clues.kinetics: Food raises exposure, about 2-fold with high-fat meals during repeated dosing. The drug is over 99% bound to plasma proteins, and about 88% of the radiolabeled dose is recovered in feces.
clues.substance: A lipophilic ester form, with a molecular weight of 349.5 for the active moiety. It is practically insoluble in water.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 250 mg uncoated and 500 mg film-coated tablets. Taken daily, with prednisone.
clues.safety: No boxed warning, and no contraindications. Fatigue and arthralgia are the most common adverse reactions, at 10% or more.
clues.indication: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, and metastatic high-risk castration-sensitive prostate cancer, each given with prednisone.
clues.mechanism: Inhibits CYP17, an enzyme in testicular, adrenal and prostate tumor tissue that is needed for androgen production, and so lowers testosterone and other androgens.

tell: A CYP17 inhibitor whose peak concentration rises about 17-fold after a single high-fat meal.
